reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, batch 3

samples_reviewed.question_text: It never bends or changes direction. Is it a straight line or a curved line?
A solid figure has a surface that bends all the way around, like a ball. What kind of surface is that?
A solid figure has a surface with no bumps or curves, like a tabletop. What kind of surface is that?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The lc asks students to identify/explain straight vs curved lines and flat vs curved surfaces; samples directly hit both halves -- 'straight line or a curved line?' and 'A solid figure has a surface that bends... what kind of surface is that?' -> curved surface.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: geometric_lines registers 6 combos across 2 axes, plausibly one axis for lines and one for 3D surfaces; my 5 samples are illustrative only, exhaustive combo execution is machine-verified separately by validate_matrix.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The longer stem ('A solid figure has a surface with no bumps or curves, like a tabletop. What kind of surface is that?') is 19 words, right at the edge of the 18-word cap, but the vocabulary and concrete tabletop/ball analogies stay grade-2 appropriate.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The 5 samples cover both named contrasts (straight-vs-curved line, flat-vs-curved surface) using different concrete referents (a ball, a tabletop), which plausibly supports mastery of both halves of this two-part competency.

competency_alignment.rationale: The content stays exactly at the identify/explain level the lc names, without drifting into naming full 3D solids (spheres, cubes) by name, which correctly keeps scope to lines and surface type only.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: There's no numeric scale involved since this is a qualitative shape-property competency, and the concrete real-world analogies (ball, tabletop) are an appropriate complexity level for grade 2 quarter 4.
